questions.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
questions.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{1} \\ -{x}_{1} \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=5 \\ -{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=3 \\ {x}_{2} &=2\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the third equation we get ${x}_{2}=2$, which we substitute into the second equation to get 

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} & =3 \\ -{x}_{1}+2 & =3 \\ {x}_{1} & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=-1$ and ${x}_{2}=2$ into the first equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} & =5 \\ -(-1)+2(2) & =5 \\ 5 & =5,\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement. 

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=-1$ and ${x}_{2}=2,$ which means

$$
-{a}_{1}+2{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-1+2=1.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 4 \\ 5\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1} \\ 5{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}4{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ 2{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 4 \\ 5\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ 5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 4 \\ 5\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=3 \\ 3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=4 \\ 5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=5\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the first equation by $3$ and adding the result to the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}13{x}_{2} & =13\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{2}=1$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+4(1) & =3\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting ${x}_{1}=1$ and ${x}_{2}=1$ into the third equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} & =5 \\ 5(1)+2(1) & =5 \\ 7 & =5,\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a false statement. 

So, the system has no solution.

questions.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ 1 \\ -4\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
questions.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ 1 \\ -4\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ -2{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2{x}_{2} \\ -3{x}_{2} \\ 5{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ 1 \\ -4\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ -2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ 1 \\ -4\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=-3 \\ -2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=1 \\ 3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} &=-4\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the first equation by $2$ and adding the resulting equations, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =-5,\end{aligned}
$$

which we substitute into the second equation to get 

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}=1 \\ -2{x}_{1}-3(-5) & =1 \\ -2{x}_{1} & =-14 \\ {x}_{1} & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=7$ and ${x}_{2}=-5$ into the third equation and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}=-4 \\ 3(7)+5(-5) & =-4 \\ -4 & =-4,\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement. 

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=7$ and ${x}_{2}=-5,$ which means

$$
7{a}_{1}-5{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=7+(-5)=2.
$$

questions.:question/problem:

$$

$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
questions.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}-7 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-9 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{1} \\ -3{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-7{x}_{2} \\ 5{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-9 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{1}-7{x}_{2} \\ -3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-9 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-7{x}_{2} &=-9 \\ -3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} &=3 \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Adding the first and the second equations we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{2} & =-6 \\ {x}_{2} & =3,\end{aligned}
$$

which we substitute into the second equation to get 

$$
\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}=3 \\ -3{x}_{1}+5(3) & =3 \\ -3{x}_{1} & =-12 \\ {x}_{1} & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=4$ and ${x}_{2}=3$ into the third equation and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=1 \\ (4)-(3) & =1 \\ 1 & =1,\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement. 

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=4$ and ${x}_{2}=3,$ which means

$$
4{a}_{1}+3{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=4+3=7.
$$

questions.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}-7 \\ -1 \\ 6\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
questions.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-7 \\ -1 \\ 6\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ -{x}_{1} \\ 2{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-7 \\ -1 \\ 6\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ 2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-7 \\ -1 \\ 6\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=-7 \\ -{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=-1 \\ 2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=6\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Adding the first and the second equation we get

$$
-2{x}_{2}=-8\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=4.
$$

Substituting ${x}_{2}=4$ into the first equation yields

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} & =-7 \\ {x}_{1}-(4) & =-7 \\ {x}_{1} & =-7+4 \\ {x}_{1} & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=-3$ and ${x}_{2}=4$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} & =6 \\ 2(-3)+3(4) & =6 \\ 6 & =6,\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement. 

So, the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=-3$ and ${x}_{2}=4,$ which means

$$
-3{a}_{1}+4{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-3+4=1.
$$

questions.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 3 \\ 4\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 4 \\ -3\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}16 \\ -1 \\ -18\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
questions.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 3 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 4 \\ -3\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}16 \\ -1 \\ -18\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-2{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1} \\ 4{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}5{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{2} \\ -3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}16 \\ -1 \\ -18\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-2{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}16 \\ -1 \\ -18\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} &=16 \\ 3{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=-1 \\ 4{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=-18\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the first equation by $3$, the second equation by $2$, and adding the resulting equations, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}15{x}_{2}+8{x}_{2} & =48-2 \\ 23{x}_{2} & =46 \\ {x}_{2} & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we substitute ${x}_{2}=2$  into the second equation to get 

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} & =-1\text{ } \\ 3{x}_{1}+4(2) & =-1 \\ 3{x}_{1} & =-9 \\ {x}_{1} & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=-3$ and ${x}_{2}=2$ into our third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} & =-18 \\ 4(-3)-3(2) & =-18 \\ -18 & =-18,\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement. 

So, the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=-3$ and ${x}_{2}=2,$ which means

$$
-3{a}_{1}+2{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(-3)+2=-1.
$$

$$

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=7 \\ -2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=9 \\ 3{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=4\end{aligned}\right.

$$

$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=3$ and ${x}_{2}=5$ into the second equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} & =9 \\ -2(3)+3(5) & =9 \\ -6+15 & =9,\end{aligned}

which gives a true statement.

$$
3{a}_{1}+5{a}_{2}=b.

$$

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2} &=-11 \\ 4{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=8 \\ 2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=-14\end{aligned}\right.

$$
\begin{aligned}6{x}_{1} & =-6 \\ {x}_{1} & =-1,\end{aligned}
$$

which we substitute into the second equation to get 

$$

{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=5+2=7.
$$

questions.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}-4 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}-14 \\ 6 \\ -5\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
questions.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}-4 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-14 \\ 6 \\ -5\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-4{x}_{1} \\ 2{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}{x}_{2} \\ 0 \\ 4{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-14 \\ 6 \\ -5\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ 2{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-14 \\ 6 \\ -5\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=-14 \\ 2{x}_{1} &=6 \\ {x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=-5\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the second equation we get ${x}_{1}=3$, which we substitute into the first equation to get 

$$
\begin{aligned}-4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} & =-14 \\ -4(3)+{x}_{2} & =-14 \\ {x}_{2} & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=3$ and ${x}_{2}=-2$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} & =-5 \\ 3+4(-2) & =-5 \\ -5 & =-5,\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement. 

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=3$ and ${x}_{2}=-2,$ which means

$$
3{a}_{1}-2{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=3+(-2)=1.
$$

questions.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ -3\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}-10 \\ 8 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
questions.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ -3\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-10 \\ 8 \\ -2\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-2{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{1} \\ -2{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}{x}_{2} \\ -2{x}_{2} \\ -3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-10 \\ 8 \\ -2\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{1}-2{x}_{2} \\ -2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-10 \\ 8 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=-10 \\ \,\,\,\,{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2} &=8 \\ -2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=-2\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the second equation by $2$ and adding that resiult to the first equation,  we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2}-4{x}_{2} & =-10+16 \\ -3{x}_{2} & =6 \\ {x}_{2} & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Now,  we substitute ${x}_{2}=-2$ into the second equation to get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2} & =8 \\ {x}_{1}-2(-2) & =8 \\ {x}_{1} & =8-4 \\ {x}_{1} & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=4$ and ${x}_{2}=-2$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} & =-2 \\ -2(4)-3(-2) & =-2 \\ -8+6 & =-2,\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement. 

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=4$ and ${x}_{2}=-2,$ which means

$$
4{a}_{1}-2{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=4-2=2.
$$

canonical_example.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors



$$
\mathbf{c_1}=\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{c_2}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{d}=\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ -5 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}.
$$



If $x_1 \mathbf{c}_1 + x_2\mathbf{c}_2  = \mathbf d,$ then what is $x_1+x_2?$
canonical_example.:question/worked-solution:
If $x_1 \mathbf{c}_1 + x_2\mathbf{c}_2  = \mathbf d,$ then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ -5 \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ -5 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=5 \\ -{x}_{1} &=-5 \\ 3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the second equation, we obtain $x_1=5,$ which we substitute into the first equation to get 

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} & =5 \\ 4(5)+{x}_{2} & =5 \\ {x}_{2} & =-15.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $x_1=5$ and $x_2=-15$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} & =0 \\ 3(5)+(-15) & =0 \\ 0 & =0,\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement. 

So the solution of the system is $x_1=5$ and $x_2=-15,$ which means

$$
5 \mathbf{c_1}-15 \mathbf{c_2} = \mathbf{d}.
$$

Consequently,

$$
x_1+x_2=5-15=-10.
$$
